newsitem.title: USA: Author's fatal illness misdiagnosed - N.Y. probe.
newsitem.headline: Author's fatal illness misdiagnosed - N.Y. probe.

text.p: Two hospitals misdiagnosed the condition of which Jonathan Larson died days before the opening of his hit Broadway musical, "Rent," a New York state investigation found.
An autopsy of the author, who posthumously received a Pulitzer Prize and a Tony Award for the show, revealed that he had a 12-inch tear in the main artery from his heart.
He died of an aneurysm at the age of 35 on Jan. 25, 1996, the night of the final rehearsal for "Rent," a modern version of "La Boheme" that depicts life on Manhattan's bohemian Lower East Side.

On Jan. 21 and 23 he had visited city hospitals complaining of severe chest pains, dizziness and shortness of breath, but he was sent home after doctors told him he had food poisoning or a viral syndrome.

In a report on its four-month probe released Thursday, the State Department of Health said his health problems were "not correctly diagnosed" and were "inappropriately treated" at Cabrini Medical Centre and St. Vincent's Medical Centre.
The department conceded that correctly diagnosing Larson's condition "would have been extremely difficult." It said his age, condition and symptoms masked the true nature of his illness.
One of the two most important risk factors for heart problems like Larson's is being older than 50, it noted.
The two hospitals were fined a total of $16,000, and doctors at both were referred to the state's Office of Professional Medical Conduct for investigation.
